source: Minchat Shai on Exod 6:10 + 6:29 (the Michlol's gate-of-letters rule; Or Torah's census)
claim_en: el-MOSHE LEMOR ('to Moses, SAYING'): the Michlol's two-sided rule, quoted whole by MS — the lamed of 'to Moses, saying' is ALWAYS dageshed (the hard letter), and the lamed of 'to Moses and to Aaron, saying' is NEVER dageshed — 'and so I found in precise manuscript books.' The stream carries BOTH halves almost whole: the compound Moses-and-Aaron stations are soft ALL FOURTEEN times (censused); the Moses-alone stations are dageshed at 77 of 79, including both in-span stations (6:10 checked here, 6:29 likewise). Or Torah ruled 'dageshed in the WHOLE Torah except ONE — the sons-of-Gad verse' (Num 32:25, which is indeed soft) — but the stream carries a SECOND soft station he did not name (the sons-of-Israel plea at Num 17:27): both softs are PLURAL human speakers pressing Moses (the sons of Gad; the we-perish plea) — the rule's engine (the divine speech-frame) holds unbroken, and the census files a discrepancy observation against Or Torah's 'only one': the tradition's rule verified at 91 of 93 stations, its two exceptions both in the people's own mouth.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:6-7 (the four tongues of redemption; the four cups)
claim_en: ve-HOTZETI... ve-HITZALTI... ve-GAALTI... ve-LAQACHTI — the FOUR TONGUES OF REDEMPTION ('I will bring out, I will deliver, I will redeem, I will take'), the Kitzur: against the FOUR KINGDOMS, and the last written ve-laqachti against EDOM — 'as a man who TAKES by force, for it is the hardest of them all'; and the four verbs' gematria = 'THIS: a poor man in Israel shall not be given fewer than FOUR CUPS' (the Passover seder's four cups drawn from this verse-pair, named): the stream carries the four as LETTER-RARITIES — the deliver-verb, the redeem-verb, and the take-verb are each the Torah's ONLY token of their form (censused: ve-hitzalti unique at 6:6, ve-gaalti unique at 6:6, ve-laqachti unique at 6:7 — checked), and the bring-out verb's whole Torah career is THREE stations, all inside this one commissioning (6:6 the promise, 7:4 the hosts, 7:5 the hand stretched out): four words the Torah spends exactly once each on this speech — plus one it spends three times, all here.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:8 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: MORASHA ('a heritage'): the heritage-word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — the LAND given as morasha here (6:8) and the TORAH given as morasha at the blessing of Moses ('Moses commanded us Torah, the HERITAGE of the congregation of Jacob,' Deut 33:4 — census checked): the Kitzur binds them — 'by the merit of the TORAH they inherited the LAND, as it is written: He gave them the lands of nations... in order that they might keep His statutes'; and the word's own grain carries the shadow: 'it is written morasha and NOT yerusha — a hint that they TRANSMIT and do not inherit: that generation would not enter the land' — the fifth promise-verb of this very speech (ve-heveti, 'and I will bring you in,' 6:8) already reading past its first hearers.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:6 (the Masorah's pair; the Sifrei)
claim_en: LAKHEN EMOR ('THEREFORE SAY'): the therefore-say formula stands exactly TWICE in the Torah (adjacency checked) — here, opening the redemption-speech to Israel, and at 'therefore say: behold I give him My covenant of PEACE' (Num 25:12 — spoken of PINCHAS): the Kitzur carries the Sifrei's ledger — 'all that Moses did, Pinchas did: Moses was made the agent to bring Israel out of Egypt, and Pinchas will be the agent to bring Israel out of the exile' — and the letter seats the pair INSIDE this chapter: the man of the second therefore-say DEBUTS at 6:25, eight verses below the first (the registry section ends on his birth): the two redeemers of the two therefore-says, both entered in one chapter's file; and lakhen = one hundred (Abraham's son at a hundred; Isaac's hundredfold; named).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:9 (the defective spelling's count)
claim_en: mi-QOTZER ruach ('from SHORTNESS of breath' — why they could not hear): written DEFECTIVE, without its vav (the Torah's only token of the form — census checked), and the Kitzur reads the missing letter's arithmetic: the lean skeleton's letters count 430 — 'to say: at the end of 430 YEARS they went out, as it is said: and it came to pass at the end of thirty years and four hundred years' (Exod 12:41's own number, six chapters early — the sojourn's total stamped inside the word for why the promise could not be heard): the people too short of breath to hear the four verbs carry, in the shortened word itself, the date on which the verbs would be kept (letters summed and checked in the build).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:13 (the Masorah's four)
claim_en: va-YETZAVEM ('and He COMMANDED them'): the command-them verb stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — the joint charge to Moses and Aaron here (6:13) and 'and he commanded them ALL that the LORD had spoken' at the descent from Sinai (Exod 34:32 — census checked); the Kitzur's Masorah counts FOUR with the Prophets' two: Yehoyada's coup-command ('this is the thing that you shall do,' 2 Kgs 11:5 — a command in the matter of BLOODSHED) and the command to the resettled Samaritans ('you shall not fear other gods,' 2 Kgs 17:35 — a command in the matter of IDOLATRY): 'so too here — Moses commanded them to keep far from idolatry and from bloodshed': the first charge of the commissioned pair, read by its three echoes as a charter against the two capital corruptions.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:24 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: ASSIR ('Assir,' first of the sons of Korach): the name stands ONCE in the Torah (census checked), and the Kitzur's Masorah pairs it with its common-noun twin — 'to bring out from the prison the BOUND (assir)' (Isa 42:7): 'this is what they said of the sons of Korach — a place was FORTIFIED for them in Gehinnom' (the tradition that Korach's sons did not die but were held on a ledge of the pit, Num 26:11's own note) — 'and this is: to bring out from prison the bound': the rebel's firstborn carries, in his one Torah station, the name of the release his line would sing (the sons-of-Korach psalms named): a prisoner's name given before the prison, redeemed after it.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:30 (the Masorah's four leaning-pairs)
claim_en: HEN ANI ('BEHOLD, I...'): the behold-I pair stands ONCE in the Torah (adjacency checked — Moses' 'behold, I am of uncircumcised lips'), and the Masorah's four leaning-stations complete it across Scripture: 'Behold, I am toward God AS YOUR MOUTH' (Job 33:6 — the Kitzur reads it as Heaven's own answer: 'do not fear the foreskin of your lips, for I will be WITH YOUR MOUTH and teach you'); 'Behold, I was left ALONE' (Isa 49:21); and 'let not the eunuch say: Behold, I am a DRY TREE' (Isa 56:3 — let him trust in the Name who healed barren Zion): the objection that closes this chapter is answered, in the Masorah's own four-row file, by the as-your-mouth verse — the same answer 4:11-12 gave in the narrative ('who made man's mouth... I will be with your mouth'), here re-issued by the concordance itself.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:3 (the finals; the gematria; the six appearances)
claim_en: va-ERA el AVRAHAM ('I APPEARED to Abraham'): the FINAL LETTERS of the opening three words — va-era / el / avraham — spell אלם ('MUTE'): the Kitzur: 'they made themselves MUTE and did not question My ways' (the fathers' silence under unkept promises, sealed into the verse that praises it — checked in the stream); and the appearing-word's file carried named: va-era in gematria = יצחק ('Isaac,' 208 — 'Isaac caused Israel to go out of Egypt,' the midrash); the vav's six = the SIX appearances written of the fathers (three to Abraham, two to Isaac, one to Jacob); and the three fathers' INITIALS in this verse — alef, yod, yod — count twenty-one, the count of אהיה ('I WILL BE,' the bush's own Name): the verse of the fathers' God carries their silence in its finals and His Name in their initials.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 6:4 (the tikkun's ruling; the printed Masorah corrected)
claim_en: eretz MEGUREHEM ('the land of their SOJOURNINGS'): written LEAN here — no vav — with the Torah-scroll tikkun MS quotes ('megurehem; another copy megurehem full — and so in the Mafteach'), and MS closes the file with his Vayishlach ruling and a warning: 'what is written in the PRINTED small Masorah here and there is an ERROR — do not rely on it' (the run's second printed-Masorah correction, after the midwives' false 'unique' at exo_01): the census verifies the skeleton's whole Torah career — the sojournings-word FULL exactly twice (Esau's departure Gen 36:7; Jacob's days-of-my-sojournings before Pharaoh Gen 47:9) and LEAN exactly once, HERE (checked): gen_59's two-full-one-lean file, opened at the Edom ledger, closes its lean station inside the covenant-verse of the land of sojournings.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 6:19 (the manuscript grammar's received rule)
claim_en: MACHLI ('Machli,' son of Merari): 'the chet takes the BARE SHEVA alone — and so NACHSHON' (6:23) — and MS cites a manuscript grammar-book: 'these are among the NAMES whose guttural letters take only the bare half-vowel, BY THE RECEIVED TRADITION' (al pi ha-qabbala): both names checked in the stream — the chet of Machli and the chet of Nachshon each on the plain sheva, no composite vowel: the corpus's half-vowel LAW gains its name-class witnesses — the sheva-vs-hataf split characterized across Genesis (stations on resh, tzadi, lamed, qof; the gutturals proven bare at ayin and he) here holds at CHET twice, inside proper names, with the tradition's own 'received' seal on exactly the reading the stream carries.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 6:23-25 (the Ramah's one-word rulings; Masekhet Soferim)
claim_en: PINCHAS enters the Torah FULL: 'and she bore him et PINCHAS' — 'full in old copies and in manuscripts, and so wrote the Ramah: written FULL with yod, and all the Torah likewise' — the census verifies it whole: four Torah stations (the debut 6:25, the zealot's rise Num 25:7, the covenant of peace Num 25:11, the war-priest Num 31:6), every one with its yod, and the LEAN skeleton standing ZERO times in the Torah (checked; MS's own cross-note sends the lean forms to Samuel's Hophni-and-Pinchas — outside the Torah's stream, named): around him the registry's one-word file — ELISHEVA one word with yod, AMMINADAV one word with yod 'and all the Torah likewise' (six stations, no lean twin anywhere; so too Masekhet Soferim), AVIHU one word, AVIASAPH one word (each the Ramah's ruling, each asserted): the priestly line is entered into the book with every name written whole.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 6:7 + 6:8 (the accent rulings)
claim_en: u-le-YAAQOV ('and to JACOB'): MS rules — 'with an ETNACHTA' (the mid-verse pause) — and the stream carries the pause exactly there (mark checked): the oath-verse rests its half-verse breath on the third father's name before turning to the giving ('and I will give it to you as a heritage: I am the LORD'); and one verse up, KI ANI ('for I am'): MS — 'ki with a GALGAL, NOT with a maqqef': the stream writes no maqqef (asserted — the ruling's no-maqqef half verified in-stream), and stores the mark as a munach — STATION TEN of the corpus's galgal class, now ten rulings deep, every station munach-in-stream: the class's standing question (does the stream's munach transcribe the galgal?) carries its tenth witness on the verse that says I-am-the-LORD.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 6:3/6:4/6:5 (named-only remainder)
claim_en: The remainder, named-only with one count-anchor: the JUXTAPOSITION the Kitzur reads across the seder-seam — 'above it is written HE SHALL DRIVE THEM OUT OF HIS LAND (6:1, the 17-word verse checked), and adjacent to it AND GOD SPOKE (6:2): teaching that the speech with him was not inside the city but outside the walled town' (the drive-out word's own exile applied to the Speaker's venue); LA-TET ('to give,' 6:4) counts 830 = 410 + 420, 'a hint to the TWO TEMPLES that stood 410 and 420 years' (the land-gift's clock, named); ASHER GARU VAH ('wherein they sojourned,' 6:4) — 'by its count, TEN TRIBES stood in the land' (named); and NAAQAT ('the groaning of,' 6:5) in the atbash cipher = the count of THE FATHERS — 'to tell you: the cry of the fathers and their prayer ascended' (named): the covenant-paragraph's four ciphers, filed under the verse whose drive-out word opens them.
